eu_ai_act.name: EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689)
eu_ai_act.note: Binding for providers and deployers placing AI systems on the EU market or whose outputs are used in the EU. Most obligations fall on high risk systems listed in Annex III, which includes creditworthiness assessment of natural persons.

aida.name: Canada AIDA (Bill C-27, Part 3)
aida.note: The Artificial Intelligence and Data Act was introduced in 2022 as part of Bill C-27 and died on the order paper when Parliament was prorogued in January 2025. Included here because it shaped Canadian expectations and because a successor bill is widely expected. Treat all references as the last published draft and companion document.

nist_ai_rmf.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (2023)
nist_ai_rmf.note: Voluntary. Organised into four functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. The Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600 1, 2024) adds actions for generative systems.

iso_42001.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023
iso_42001.note: AI management system standard. Clauses 4 to 10 set the management system, Annex A lists controls, Annex B gives implementation guidance.

osfi_e23.name: OSFI Guideline E-23 Model Risk Management (2025)
osfi_e23.note: Applies to federally regulated financial institutions in Canada from May 2027. Expands the 2017 version to cover all models including AI and machine learning, and introduces a model lifecycle with risk based intensity.

colorado_ai_act.name: Colorado AI Act (SB 24-205)
colorado_ai_act.note: Covers developers and deployers of high risk AI systems that make or are a substantial factor in consequential decisions, including lending and financial services. Effective date was pushed to June 30, 2026 by SB 25B 004.

themes.name: Risk classification and scoping
themes.description: Deciding whether a system falls in scope and at what risk tier.

eu_ai_act.ref: Art. 6 and Annex III; Art. 5 prohibited practices
eu_ai_act.text: Classify the system against the prohibited list and the Annex III high risk use cases. Creditworthiness and insurance pricing for natural persons are high risk.

aida.ref: s. 7 and proposed regulations on high impact systems
aida.text: Assess whether the system is a high impact system under the regulations. The companion document named decisions about services, employment and credit.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Establish context, intended purpose and the level of risk the organisation is willing to tolerate.

iso_42001.ref: Clause 6.1.2 and A.5 AI system impact assessment
iso_42001.text: Run an AI risk assessment and an impact assessment proportionate to the system.

osfi_e23.text: Assign a model risk rating that drives the intensity of validation and monitoring.

colorado_ai_act.ref: s. 6-1-1701(9) definition of high risk AI system
colorado_ai_act.text: Determine if the system makes or is a substantial factor in a consequential decision.

themes.name: Data governance and quality
themes.description: Controls over training, validation and test data including representativeness and lawful basis.

eu_ai_act.text: Training, validation and testing data must meet quality criteria, be examined for bias and be relevant and representative.

aida.ref: s. 6 anonymised data; s. 8 measures to identify and mitigate risk
aida.text: Establish measures for how anonymised data is used and mitigate risks of harm and biased output.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Document data provenance, representativeness and test set independence.

iso_42001.text: Controls on data acquisition, quality, provenance and preparation.

osfi_e23.text: Data used in models must be fit for purpose, traceable and controlled; expectations scale with model risk.

colorado_ai_act.text: Developers must describe the data used to train the system and known limitations.

themes.name: Technical documentation and model cards
themes.description: Written description of the system, its purpose, design, performance and limits.

eu_ai_act.text: Technical documentation covering general description, development process, monitoring, performance metrics and risk management.

aida.ref: s. 11 record keeping and s. 12 publication of plain language description
aida.text: Keep records of mitigation measures and publish a plain language description of a high impact system.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Document the system, its intended uses and evaluation methods; model cards and datasheets are named practices.

iso_42001.text: Maintain documented information on the AI system through its lifecycle.

osfi_e23.text: Model documentation must allow an independent party to understand and replicate the model.

colorado_ai_act.text: Developers must give deployers documentation on intended use, data, performance, limitations and known risks of algorithmic discrimination.

themes.name: Human oversight
themes.description: People can understand, intervene in and override the system.

eu_ai_act.text: High risk systems must be designed for effective oversight; deployers must assign oversight to competent people.

aida.text: The companion document listed human oversight among expected mitigation measures; the bill itself did not specify.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Define roles for human oversight and mechanisms to override or decommission.

iso_42001.ref: A.9.3 and B.9.3 responsible use, human oversight
iso_42001.text: Determine where human oversight is needed and how it is exercised.

osfi_e23.ref: Section 3 model use and ongoing management
osfi_e23.text: Model users must understand model limits and have procedures for override when outputs are unreliable.

colorado_ai_act.ref: s. 6-1-1703(4) right to appeal to human review
colorado_ai_act.text: Consumers may appeal an adverse consequential decision for human review where technically feasible.

themes.name: Transparency to affected persons
themes.description: Telling people that AI is used and explaining decisions that affect them.

eu_ai_act.text: Instructions for use, notice to natural persons subject to high risk decisions, chatbot disclosure, and a right to explanation of individual decisions.

aida.text: Publish a plain language description of how the system is used and the decisions it makes.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Transparency and explainability are listed trustworthiness characteristics to be measured.

iso_42001.text: Provide information on the AI system to users and affected parties.

osfi_e23.text: Explainability expectations rise with model risk, but the guideline speaks to internal users rather than customers.

colorado_ai_act.text: Deployers must notify consumers before a consequential decision, give reasons for adverse decisions and disclose interaction with AI.

themes.name: Bias and fairness testing
themes.description: Testing for discriminatory outcomes before and after deployment.

eu_ai_act.text: Examine data for possible biases that lead to discrimination and take measures to detect and correct them.

aida.ref: s. 8 and definition of biased output in s. 5
aida.text: Establish measures to identify, assess and mitigate risks of biased output.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Fairness and bias are evaluated and results documented.

iso_42001.ref: A.5.4 and B.5.4 impact assessment on individuals and groups
iso_42001.text: Assess impacts on individuals and groups including fairness.

osfi_e23.ref: Section 3 validation and Annex on AI/ML
osfi_e23.text: Validation should test for unintended bias where models affect customers; expectations align with conduct obligations.

colorado_ai_act.text: Deployers must complete an impact assessment covering known or foreseeable risks of algorithmic discrimination.

themes.name: Post deployment monitoring
themes.description: Ongoing tracking of performance, drift and harms after go live.

eu_ai_act.text: Providers must run a post market monitoring system; deployers must monitor operation per instructions.

aida.text: Monitor compliance with mitigation measures and their effectiveness.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Monitor deployed systems and track risks over time.

iso_42001.ref: Clause 9.1 and A.6.2.6 operation and monitoring
iso_42001.text: Monitor, measure and evaluate AI system performance in operation.

osfi_e23.text: Ongoing monitoring with thresholds and escalation, frequency set by model risk rating.

colorado_ai_act.ref: s. 6-1-1703(2)(c) annual review of impact assessment
colorado_ai_act.text: Impact assessments must be reviewed at least annually and after substantial modification.

themes.name: Incident reporting
themes.description: Reporting serious failures or harms to regulators or affected parties.

eu_ai_act.text: Providers report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities within set deadlines.

aida.text: Notify the Minister as soon as feasible if use of the system results or is likely to result in material harm.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Processes for incident response and sharing incident information.

iso_42001.text: Treat AI incidents as nonconformities and keep event logs.

osfi_e23.text: Escalate model failures internally; regulatory reporting flows through existing OSFI incident expectations.

colorado_ai_act.text: Developers and deployers must notify the Attorney General within 90 days of discovering algorithmic discrimination.

themes.name: Third party and vendor management
themes.description: Oversight of models, APIs and components bought or licensed from others.

eu_ai_act.ref: Art. 25 and Art. 53 for general purpose model providers
eu_ai_act.text: Responsibilities along the value chain; deployers that substantially modify become providers.

aida.text: The draft placed obligations on whoever makes the system available or manages its operation, without a separate vendor regime.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Policies for third party software, data and models, including contingency when they fail.

iso_42001.ref: A.10 third party and customer relationships
iso_42001.text: Allocate responsibilities with suppliers and ensure supplier processes meet the organisation's requirements.

osfi_e23.ref: Section 3 and link to Guideline B-10
osfi_e23.text: Vendor and open source models are in scope; institutions remain accountable for validation and monitoring.

colorado_ai_act.text: Developers must furnish deployers with the information needed for impact assessments.

themes.name: Record keeping and logging
themes.description: Automatic logs and retention so decisions can be reconstructed.

eu_ai_act.text: Automatic logging over the lifetime; providers and deployers keep logs at least six months.

aida.text: Keep records of the assessment, mitigation measures and monitoring.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Keep records of risk management decisions and evaluation results.

iso_42001.text: Control documented information and log events through operation.

osfi_e23.text: Maintain an enterprise model inventory with status, rating and ownership.

colorado_ai_act.text: Retain impact assessments and records for at least three years after final deployment.

themes.name: Accountability and governance roles
themes.description: Named owners, senior oversight and an internal control structure.

eu_ai_act.text: Risk management system and quality management system for providers; deployer duties.

aida.text: An accountability framework with roles, training and policies was expected to be set by regulation.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Policies, roles and senior accountability for AI risk.

iso_42001.text: Top management commitment, policy and defined roles.

osfi_e23.text: Senior management owns the model risk framework; independent review function; clear model owner, developer, validator roles.

colorado_ai_act.text: Deployers must adopt a risk management policy and program; NIST AI RMF or ISO 42001 are named as reference frameworks.

themes.name: Generative and general purpose model duties
themes.description: Extra obligations when the system uses a general purpose or generative model.

eu_ai_act.text: Mark synthetic content; general purpose model providers keep technical documentation, copyright policy and training summary; systemic risk models face evaluation and incident duties.

aida.text: Proposed amendments would have added obligations for general purpose systems and machine learning models.

nist_ai_rmf.text: Actions for confabulation, information integrity, harmful content and data privacy specific to generative systems.

iso_42001.text: No generative specific controls; general controls apply.

osfi_e23.ref: Annex on AI and machine learning models
osfi_e23.text: Generative models are models; explainability and monitoring expectations are heightened where outputs are not deterministic.

colorado_ai_act.text: Consumers must be told when they are interacting with an AI system.
